question: Which of the following is NOT the socio-economic objective of Industrial Policy Statement 1980?

options.text: Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality
Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment

solution:
The correct answer is __**Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 emphasized **enhancing productivity, employment generation, and the optimum utilization of existing production capacity**.
 
• It aimed at the **promotion of export-oriented industries** to improve foreign exchange earnings.
 
• The policy also focused on **consumer protection against high prices and poor quality** of goods.
 
• **Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment (FDI)** was not a primary objective of the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Statement 1980**

 
 
• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 was introduced to revitalize the Indian economy and make it more competitive.
 
• The policy emphasized modernization, technological upgradation, and the development of small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
 
• It aimed at achieving higher growth rates and industrial diversification to reduce regional disparities.
 
• The policy also sought to improve the efficiency of public sector enterprises and increase their contribution to the economy.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**
 
 
• FDI involves investment from a foreign entity into the business interests of another country.
 
• It is a significant source of non-debt financial resources for the economic development of a country.
 
• FDI brings in capital, technology, and expertise, and can lead to job creation and infrastructure development.
 
• While FDI is important, it was not the main focus of the Industrial Policy of 1980, which was more oriented towards self-reliance and domestic industrial growth.
